subject: Exec workshop: guest billing & virtual card gap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-06T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Exec workshop: guest billing & virtual card gap

Team —

Quick heads-up: Acme is sending 7 external executive guests for the Nov 12 onsite. Hotel (Granview) is asking for a guaranteed card for incidentals and they require an $800 pre-authorization per room at check-in. We booked on the Redwood virtual vendor card that we usually use for venues, but the authorization bounced this morning with a decline code pointing to an MCC mismatch.

Attachments: hotel_reservation_1112_stub.pdf (reservation confirmation), guest_list_acme.xlsx

Impact: if we can’t guarantee the rooms, Acme may ask to move or we could lose the executive suite block. Please advise on whether Finance can:
- Increase the virtual card ceiling for this vendor so Granview can complete the preauth, OR
- Approve a one-time charge on the Redwood corporate (physical) card for guarantee, OR
- Confirm that guests can check-in with pre-paid incidentals covered by the venue (unlikely).

I’m looping Monica for operations details and Marcus for finance. This is high priority — hotel needs a guaranteed card by EOD today to keep the block.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Partnerships Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exec workshop: guest billing & virtual card gap

Jordan / Monica —

Thanks for flagging. The authorization declined because the MCC on file for Granview doesn’t match the merchant category we locked for vendor virtual cards (hotel vs. conference services). Two quick points:

1) We can create a one-off vendor virtual card with a higher preauth ceiling, but Procurement needs a completed form and a PO number for anything over $5k. I’m attaching the procurement_form_signed.pdf — if you can confirm cost-center and PO I’ll issue the card.

2) Alternative is to have Redwood pay the guarantee on the corporate card and then bill Acme via a hosted invoice. That requires manager approval and will take ~24 hours to post.

Short-term recommendation: If Acme is OK with us covering the preauth and billing them, Lauren can approve the exception and I’ll push a single-use virtual card bound to Granview. If not, guests may need to provide personal cards at check-in.

Attachment: procurement_form_signed.pdf

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exec workshop: guest billing & virtual card gap

Looping in operations context: Granview’s events team confirmed the block and said their policy is a pre-authorization equal to two nights plus $150 incidentals per room. For our late check-ins (some flights land after midnight) they will not hold rooms without a guaranteed card.

I called Grace at reservations and asked for a 48-hour hold while we sort payment; she said she needs a guaranteed card by close of business today to maintain the executive suite adjacent rooms together.

If Finance can spin up the vendor-specific virtual card now, please include the vendor MCC override so the auth goes through. If Lauren approves corporate charge instead, I’ll share check-in instructions and update the guest list.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Events & Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exec workshop: guest billing & virtual card gap

Approved — one-time exception.

I authorize Finance to issue a single-use vendor virtual card with an increased pre-auth ceiling to cover the required room incidentals and the $800 preauth per room. Marcus, please:
- Create virtual card named "ACME-Workshop-11-2026" bound to Granview Hotel (MCC override to hotels)
- Limit to the exact preauth total + $500 buffer, single use, force vendor binding
- Tag cost center: ENG-TRAVEL; Project tag: ACME-ONSITE

Jordan/Monica: confirm final room count to calculate total and I’ll sign off on any residual difference up to $1,000. Please confirm by 16:00 PT.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Grace Park <reservations@granviewhotel.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Granview Hotel Accounting <ar@granview.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exec workshop: guest billing & virtual card gap

Hi Jordan / Monica —

Thanks for confirming. We were able to process the pre-authorization using the vendor virtual card "ACME-Workshop-11-2026" this morning. Attached is a stub invoice showing the guaranteed amounts per room; final incidentals will post at check-out.

Attachments: hotel_invoice_1112_stub.pdf

Checking in: please provide estimated arrival windows so we can pre-print keys. Breakfast vouchers included for each executive — we’ll hold the suite block until arrival.

Best,
Grace Park
Group Reservations | Granview Hotel
